description: The image displays two pie charts comparing performance outcomes across two categories—likely representing different models or conditions—based on the paper “Laying the Foundation First: Investigating the Generalization from Atomic Skills to Complex Reasoning Tasks.” The legend identifies three outcome types: “Atomic Skill Fail” (dark teal), “Correct” (medium teal), and “Reason Error” (light gray). In the left pie chart, “Atomic Skill Fail” dominates at 68.0%, followed by “Correct” and “Reason Error” each at 12.0%, and a small unlabeled white segment at 8.0%. The right pie chart shows a more balanced distribution: “Correct” is largest at 55.0%, followed by “Reason Error” at 21.0%, “Atomic Skill Fail” at 10.0%, and an unlabeled white segment at 14.0%. The charts visually contrast a scenario where atomic skill failure is predominant (left) with one where correct responses are more frequent (right), suggesting improved generalization or performance in the latter case. The unlabeled white segments may represent a fourth category not defined in the legend, possibly “Other” or “Unspecified.”
